title: Trellis-based prefix catalog and stitched KV allocator for inter-request deduplication
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem: High-rate, interleaved conversational traffic leaves many small, overlapping prompt prefixes resident in GPU KV caches causing fragmentation, duplicated token embeddings, and inefficient slab utilization. Goal: Reduce GPU KV memory waste and backend token compute by detecting shared prefix fragments across concurrent and recent requests and reusing a canonicalized fragment store. Success metrics: 20% reduction in active KV memory footprint for mixed conversational workloads, 12% lower median p95 token compute, and no regression on tail latency for small requests.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Trellis prefix catalog: a lightweight graph index that tracks prefix fragment equivalence classes across recent requests and a stitched KV allocator that packs deduplicated fragments into contiguous GPU slabs. The runtime will consult the catalog during request admission to map incoming prompt segments to canonical fragments and update refcounts atomically. Background compaction reclaims fragmentation and performs opportunistic relocations when slab occupancy crosses thresholds. Provide graceful fallback to per-request copy when fragments are pinned or a refcount mismatch is detected.
technical_details: Data structures: Trellis catalog is a sharded, time-partitioned index where nodes represent canonical prefix fragments and edges capture continuation probability and usage co-occurrence. Each node stores fragment fingerprint, token-length, refcount, GPU slab id, slab offset, and last-used timestamp.

Allocation: Stitched allocator manages slab segments with micro-slots for variable-length fragments. When inserting, allocator prefers exact-fit or buddy-fit placements to minimize internal fragmentation and records placement in the Trellis node.

Admission path changes: During continuous batching admission, we split incoming prompts into canonicalizable segments (prefix tokens aligned to tokenizer boundaries), compute short fingerprint hashes, and query the Trellis for matches. Hits increment refcounts and point the request at the slab offset; misses allocate new fragment slots and schedule compute to materialize KV for that fragment.

Consistency: Use optimistic insertion with epoch tokens. Workers attempt to insert a fragment and publish a small commit record. If a concurrent insertion raced, the loser reconciles by pointing to the winner’s slab location and releasing its temporary allocation.

Eviction: Hybrid time-aware LRU with occupancy credits. Hot fragments gain credit boosting residency; low-utility fragments are compacted by background compaction into contiguous regions and then freed.

Compaction: Background compaction runs per-shard, copying live fragments into fresh slabs in the same GPU (to avoid inter-GPU transfer) and updates Trellis mappings under a short mutex to minimize admission stalls.

Metrics & tracing: Track fragment_hit_rate, slab_utilization, bytes_saved_by_dedupe, avg_refcount, compaction_time, and admission_latency_bump. Add tracing spans on catalog lookup and stitch operations and surface in console-2026 dashboards.
API changes: Add per-request advisory flags: allow_fragment_reuse (default true), prefer_inplace_allocation (for low-latency pinning), and reuse_tolerance_ms (how old a fragment can be for reuse).
migration_plan: Spike (done): Proof-of-concept Trellis index and microbench harness on a single GPU; validated 28% peak memory reduction on synthetic conversational trace.

Phase 1 (canary): Deploy stitched allocator and Trellis in canary runtime on a small fleet; enable reuse_tolerance_ms=500 and allow_fragment_reuse=true for non-critical traffic. Monitor slab_utilization and admission_latency_bump.
Phase 2 (gradual rollout): Expand to 25% of serving capacity with progressive lowering of reuse_tolerance_ms to 200ms and enable compaction jobs at low-priority scheduling windows.
Phase 3 (opt-in for Dedicated customers): Add controls in console for fragment reuse policies, and provide an opt-out toggle for customers who prefer deterministic per-request KV residency.
Fallback: If p95 latency increases >5% or error rate regresses, auto-disable reuse for that model and rollback compaction jobs while capturing traces for postmortem.
risks: Race conditions in concurrent fragment insertion leading to double allocations and transient refcount spikes. Mitigation: optimistic commits with reconciliation and strong post-insert validation in the admission path.
Compaction overhead can compete for GPU cycles and increase tail latency. Mitigation: run compaction only when slab_utilization > 70% and throttle using runtime admission crediting.
Cross-tenant leakage if fragment canonicalization is too permissive. Mitigation: include tenant-scoped namespace in Trellis keys and enforce strict ACL when mixing fragments from different tenants.
Instrumentation gap: insufficient visibility into fragment-level costs may hide regressions. Mitigation: instrument fine-grained metrics before rollout and run A/B with production prompts.
Complexity for deterministic replay/eviction during debugging. Mitigation: add a debug mode that forces per-request allocations and snapshot Trellis state on demand.
updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed — implemented Trellis prototype and micro-bench harness. Observed 28% peak KV memory reduction on synthetic conversational trace; small increase (~2%) in admission latency during heavy contention.
2026-02-28: Design review with runtime and infra. Decision: use optimistic insertion + reconciliation instead of a global lock to keep admission path latency predictable.
2026-03-04: Built stitched allocator prototype; validated reduced fragmentation on variable-length fragment mixes. Added unit tests for buddy-fit placement and mismatch reconcile.
2026-03-08: Safety audit with security team — confirmed tenant scoping required. Added tenant namespace to Trellis keys; integration tests updated.
2026-03-10: Canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-15 on a 10-node canary fleet. Monitoring playbook drafted; SRE oncall assigned for the first 72 hours.
